A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BiPRM by the same authors and retain identifiable methods and experiments. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–B in v1 and A–E in v2 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Best-of-N experiments, directional ablations, and scored qualitative examples, including detailed results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports revised Best-of-N experiments and original ProcessBench evaluations, ensemble comparisons, diagnostic analyses, sensitivity results, and inference measurements.

M1.justification: V1 averages L2R and R2L rewards with fixed equal weights. V2 introduces an MLP gate using concatenated hidden states to learn step-dependent fusion weights (Section 3.2, Equations 4–5). This changes a central inference component and introduces trainable parameters; prompt reversal and the three training objectives remain.

E1.justification: V2 retains Math-Shepherd training and GSM-Plus/MATH500 solution selection, while adding ProcessBench's 3,400 examples across GSM8K, MATH, Omni-MATH, and OlympiadBench. First-error localization and flawless-solution identification substantially extend evaluation beyond selecting correct final answers.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 adds independently trained 2×L2R and 2×R2L ensemble comparators to test the computational-budget alternative. V1's fixed-average BiPRM becomes the 'w/o Dynamic' comparator against the new gated method. L2R and directional-removal comparisons remain, while the new case-study tables also report R2L scores.

E3.justification: V2 adds first-error/flawless-solution F1 evaluation, compute-matched ensemble controls, normalized-position MAE analysis, aggregation-operator comparisons, and single-solution latency measurement. Appendix A also changes the stated gradient accumulation from 6 to 4. This is a reported training-setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that all retained baseline experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's directional ablations, v2 tests dynamic versus static fusion and homogeneous ensembles, analyzes positional errors and gating weights, and compares four aggregation operators. The fries case is replaced by scored induction, calculation-error, and arithmetic-disconnect examples, including an explicit R2L failure case in Appendix D.

E5.justification: V2 Table 4 newly specifies that the two-model ensembles use independently trained PRMs with different seeds. Both versions otherwise list seed 1106. Neither reports confidence intervals, run-to-run variability, or formal significance tests; the ensemble disclosure does not establish repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Many BiPRM BON scores are replaced: for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B with Llama-3-70B-Instruct sampling and BCE, MATH500 average accuracy changes from 44.00 to 48.48. Because the method and stated training settings change, this does not isolate a same-setting gain. V2 also adds ProcessBench results, averaging 30.2 F1 versus 24.6 for L2R, and ensemble, sensitivity, diagnostic, and timing results.

T1.justification: V2 defines the learned gate and weighted reward and revises the corresponding gradient expression. Equation 2 corrects the future-step range from starting at 0 to starting at 1. No theorem or proof is added. The revised Equation 6 omits the derivative contribution from the input-dependent gate.

C1.justification: The central efficiency claim changes from no additional parameters or latency to approximately 0.3% additional parameters and 5% latency. The abstract now emphasizes adaptive fusion and explicit error localization, replacing the up-to-31.9% improvement statement with average relative gains of 10.6% across solution-level configurations and 37.7% across step-level settings.

C2.justification: V2 develops position-dependent explanations for directional reliability and adaptive gating. New limitations acknowledge doubled FLOPs, unverified generalization beyond mathematics, and R2L failures on locally inconsistent arithmetic. Appendix E also explains retaining minimum aggregation despite the mean operator's slight overall empirical advantage.

D1.justification: V2 documents batching forward and reversed inputs together, the single-RTX-A5000 timing setup, and the gate's 0.005B parameter overhead. It adds a promise to release code after acceptance and revises gradient accumulation. Most software and training details are retained or relocated, while v1's explicit scalar reward-head description is removed.

R1.justification: V2 introduces an explicit novelty distinction from BiRM (Chen et al., 2025), contrasting auxiliary future-value prediction with reversed-context verification, and adds ProcessBench's citation. It substantially narrows the literature coverage by removing discussions and citations concerning dual-model pretraining, non-autoregressive generation, and models such as ULMFiT, XLNet, and T5.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, inference description, results narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized around solution-level and step-level evaluation rather than backbone-specific reporting. The case-study subsection becomes a broader analysis section, with a new limitations section and expanded appendix organization.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn and Figure 3 adds error and gating plots. Main results are consolidated into an averaged table, with detailed Qwen results moved to Appendix C. New diagnostic, timing, and sensitivity tables accompany redesigned case-study tables with separate label and model-score columns. Typography and page layout also change.

improvement.justification: V1 supports step-level benefits mainly through solution-ranking results and a qualitative example. V2 adds direct ProcessBench diagnostics, controls for increased computation, fusion and aggregation analyses, measured latency, and substantive failure/domain limitations. These resolve important evidential and transparency gaps. The gains outweigh remaining defects, including the incomplete gate-gradient expression and conflicting Qwen/Llama/Q-value MATH500 scores of 47.80 and 48.92 in v2 Tables 2 and 13.
